data.title: President berates countries that ‘insult’ Indonesia over toxic haze
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesia’s president lashed out on Wednesday against “countries that like to insult” his nation over wildfires that have razed vast areas, spewing toxic haze into neighbouring countries.

data.title: Japan sends senior diplomat to Russia over detained journalist
data.description: TOKYO — Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist detained by Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said on Wednesday.

data.title: Record-late 30°C heat grips wide swathe of Japan
data.description: KYODO — A wide swath of Japan faced sweltering heat on Wednesday, with temperatures in some regions recording the latest day in the year to top 30 degrees Celsius, prompting many to switch back to summer clothes for the day.

data.title: North Korea says 'new firepower units' in place after border threat
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea has moved new units into "firing positions", the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un said Wednesday, days after Pyongyang warned it was considering deploying additional strike means to its border with South Korea.

data.title: UK approves new North Sea gas drilling
data.description: LONDON - The UK government said on Wednesday that it had approved plans to begin drilling in a controversial new gas field in the North Sea, ending months of speculation about the future of the site.

data.title: 'Daily struggle': Cubans dig wells in search of water
data.description: HAVANA — Kevin Martinez has come up with a creative new way to avoid shutting his restaurant when water runs low in Cuba, a common source of frustration for the business owner.

data.title: Malaysia bans civil servants from using Israeli mapping app
data.description: KUALA ​LUMPUR — Malaysia has banned civil servants ​from using Alphabet's navigation application Waze after Prime ​Minister Anwar Ibrahim ‌said its origins in Israel raised security concerns.

data.title: World falling 'dangerously short' on climate action: UN chief
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century, the UN warned on Wednesday.

data.title: South Korea launches new bid to guide crowd-pulling shark to sea
data.description: SEOUL - South Korean authorities began a new attempt Wednesday to coax a shark-turned-viral sensation back to sea, with falling temperatures in the Busan canal where it is stranded raising concerns for its survival.

data.title: US envoy to meet Russia's president after 'productive' talks with Zelensky
data.description: SAINT PETERSBURG — US envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Saint Petersburgand meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday following "very productive" talks with Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.

data.title: French PM to meet unions as government prepares for more protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France's prime minister plans to meet unions on Wednesday to discuss security and has vowed a "massive" police deployment at protests, following riots in the past week that led to curfews and arrests.

data.title: 'To the shelter, quickly!' Air raids reshape Kyiv school life
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - When the air raid alert sounded over the Kyiv region, children knew exactly what to do: they grabbed their tiny backpacks and ran towards the shelter, abandoning bikes, toys and even a doll on the school playground.

data.title: Musk backs SpaceX-Tesla merger as rocket firm turns profit
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Elon Musk said Tuesday he would back a merger of SpaceX and Tesla, as his rocket and AI company reported its first quarterly profit since going public, driven by deals to rent out computing power to AI firms.

data.title: Meta says it complied with Brazil court order to treat candidates equally
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - US tech giant Meta said Tuesday it had complied with a Brazilian court order to treat the election campaigns of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro equally.

data.title: Alberta separatists vow to fight on, risking turmoil for Canada
data.description: EDMONTON (CANADA) - Separatists in Canada's Alberta province say their independence fight is not over despite a decisive referendum loss, risking long-term political turmoil in an oil-rich province crucial to the Canadian economy.

data.title: Trump says he wants Zelensky to 'make a deal' with Russia
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump on Tuesday urged Volodymyr Zelensky to make a deal with Russia -- redoubling pressure on the Ukrainian leader even as Moscow grinds on with the war it launched four years ago.

data.title: Italy sends troops, toughens security laws after Milan clashes
data.description: ROME - Italy on Tuesday approved the deployment of 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes as fuel price protests hit pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy.

data.title: All who profited from fund scandal 'identified': Turkish minister
data.description: ISTANBUL - Everyone who profited from the sprawling multi-billion dollar investment fund scandal gripping Turkey has been identified, Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said on Tuesday, expressing confidence the markets would emerge stronger from the controversy.

data.title: Global warming pace accelerating, says climate scientist
data.description: LONDON - Global warming caused by fossil fuel emissions is accelerating, ​pushing many ⁠of the Earth’s most important ecosystems close to their tipping points, according to a leading climate scientist.

data.title: Indonesian anger builds over wildfires and toxic haze
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesians protested in several cities on Tuesday, raging against wildfires and a toxic haze that has made thousands unwell for weeks on end in a crisis that has engulfed Southeast Asia.

data.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada
data.description: CALGARY - Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province’s first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the United States.

data.title: Unhappy republic: France’s troubles extend beyond the street
data.description: PARIS - “Revolution!” some shouted during France’s protests. Others demanded better classroom conditions. Many simply wanted their household budgets to stop shrinking as fuel and food prices spike.

data.title: UN says 19 million Afghans facing ‘acute food insecurity’
data.description: GENEVA - The number of people facing acute food insecurity in Afghanistan is set to rise above 19 million during the forthcoming winter season, the United Nations warned on Tuesday.

data.title: Zelensky and US envoys seek to repair frayed ties
data.description: OSLO - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing to hold talks with top US envoys in Norway on Tuesday in a bid to get strained relations with Washington “on a more constructive path”, Oslo said.

data.title: North Korea releases Kim photos to counter death rumours
data.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has appeared in photographs released by state media during a visit to a clothing exhibition, as speculation about his health and rumoured death circulates online.

data.title: Rubio lands in India for ‘trade diplomacy’
data.description: MUMBAI - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday, his second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade.

data.title: Settler violence becomes a liability for Israeli PM
data.description: JERUSALEM - Attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank have turned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s championing of settlers into a potential liability days before elections, with opponents calling him soft on “Jewish terrorism”.

data.title: France to impose new curfews where necessary: PM
data.description: PARIS — France will impose new curfews in areas where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had "helped keep the night calm".

data.title: Indonesia investigates crash of suspected Chinese rocket fragment
data.description: JAKARTA — Indonesian authorities were investigating on Tuesday after a car-sized piece of what a government agency said was a Chinese space rocket crashed into a palm oil plantation near homes and work sites.

data.title: ‘Online echo chamber’ amplifies political violence threats in Australia
data.description: SYDNEY - Australia’s security chiefs had warned of “online echo chambers” fuelling grievances and conspiracies and stepped up prosecutions for threats of political violence ahead of Monday’s attack on a lawmaker in a rural town.

data.title: South Korea to reduce Ukraine embassy staff after PoW row
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea's foreign ministry said on Tuesday it would withdraw some staff from its embassy in Ukraine, as a diplomatic row deepens over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul.

data.title: Seoul warns of ‘firm’ response to North Korea’s border threats
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea’s military warned Tuesday of a “firm” response and resolute punishment for any further provocations by North Korea, saying it was “unacceptable” for Pyongyang to blame Seoul for escalating tensions.

data.title: Too much of a good scent? Hanoi trims iconic trees
data.description: HANOI - Vietnam's capital Hanoi has launched a large-scale programme to prune hundreds of its iconic blackboard trees and is considering relocating some after their distinctive fragrance proved too much for some residents.

data.title: Curfew imposed in parts of Paris
data.description: PARIS - ⁠French ​authorities imposed a night curfew on the Place de la Republique ​and streets around ‌Les Halles in Paris from ⁠2000 GMT on Monday night (3am Tuesday, Thailand) until 0400 ​GMT on Tuesday, French ​broadcaster BFM ‌reported, ​following riots over the weekend amid nationwide protests.

data.title: Hong Kong police arrest woman after dog thrown into sea
data.description: A woman has been arrested on suspicion of animal cruelty after allegedly throwing a dog into the sea in Hong Kong.
